title: A forgiving parser
summary: Turn messy typing into clean commands.

steps.title: Stage 2: the parser
body: Real players type `n`, `go to the north`, `L`, or press Enter by accident. A **parser** turns any of that into a clean `(verb, noun)` pair, so the game loop only deals with tidy commands.
Separating *parsing* from *acting* is the same idea as model binding in ASP.NET: one layer turns raw input into a request, the next handles it. It also makes the parser easy to test on its own.

code: words = [w for w in line.lower().split() if w not in FILLER]
for line in ["N", "go to the east", "l", "take the lamp", "   ", "go d", "dance wildly"]:
steps.explain: Filler words are dropped, aliases and one-letter directions are expanded, and a bare direction becomes a `go`.

steps.prompt: Complete the alias lookup so unknown verbs pass through unchanged.

steps.title: Plug in the parser
prompt: Your code from stage 1 is in the editor. Add:
- lowercase, split, and drop the filler words `the`, `to`, `a`, `an`
- `n s e w u d` mean `north south east west up down`, both as a verb (`n`) and after `go` (`go n`)
- the noun is the remaining words joined by spaces (`""` if none); blank input gives `("", "")`
- `read_command()`: `parse(input())`, but return `("quit", "")` if input runs out (`EOFError`).
Then make the loop use it. New behaviour: blank lines are ignored silently, `go` alone prints `Go where?`. Everything from stage 1 must still work.
steps.starter:
ROOMS = {
    "hall": {
        "name": "Hall",
        "desc": "A dusty hall with a grand staircase.",
        "exits": {"north": "library", "east": "kitchen"},
        "items": ["lamp"],
    },
    "library": {
        "name": "Library",
        "desc": "Shelves of old books line the walls.",
        "exits": {"south": "hall"},
        "items": ["key", "book"],
    },
    "kitchen": {
        "name": "Kitchen",
        "desc": "It smells of old bread. A trapdoor leads down.",
        "exits": {"west": "hall", "down": "cellar"},
        "items": [],
    },
    "cellar": {
        "name": "Cellar",
        "desc": "Dark and damp. Something glints in the corner.",
        "exits": {"up": "kitchen"},
        "items": ["treasure"],
        "locked": True,
    },
}


def describe(room_id):
    room = ROOMS[room_id]
    print(f"== {room['name']} ==")
    print(room["desc"])
    print("Exits: " + ", ".join(sorted(room["exits"])))


current = "hall"
describe(current)
while True:
    words = input().strip().lower().split()
    match words:
        case ["look"]:
            describe(current)
        case ["go", direction]:
            exits = ROOMS[current]["exits"]
            if direction in exits:
                current = exits[direction]
                describe(current)
            else:
                print("You can't go that way.")
        case ["quit"]:
            print("Bye.")
            break
        case _:
            print("I don't understand.")

hints: Filter filler words with a comprehension, then `verb, *rest = words`.
Look up the verb in `ALIASES`, then in `DIRECTIONS`; if it is now a direction, return `("go", verb)`.
In the loop, `match verb, noun:` with `case "go", "":` before `case "go", direction:`.
